answer: At most 2 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a onyx tag. The canyon cap is enforced at intake and quartz exposes the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool therefore cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch whatever the capital it holds, because every participant consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 26 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
